summary.headline: SRG Housing management denies Rs 400 crore siphoning report and NHB red flag; no hard financials or audit timeline given on the 16 Sep 2026 call.
summary.overview:
This was a clarification call, not an earnings call, held after an Economic Times article (10 Sep 2026) alleged Rs 400 crore of promoter-linked diversion and NPA manipulation. The MD denied all allegations and said the NHB red flag is part of a routine supervisory audit that began in July 2026, with no reasons yet shared. He cited a 39.21% capital adequacy ratio, 25% QoQ PAT growth, and no delays on lender obligations, but gave no amount for collections or liquidity. New disbursements have been slowed, the board has resolved to convert from a housing finance company to an NBFC, and promoters raised their stake by 1%.</overview>

segments.name: Housing loans (core)
segments.commentary: Management says part disbursements continue but new business is slow and sanctions from banks are pending. Management said it has not shared exact disbursement or sanction figures.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a slowdown in Q2 FY27 from fresh sanctions and disbursements, with Q3 and Q4 'good'.

Management expects the NHB audit to close 'soon'; asked whether it would close in 1-2 months, the MD said '100%'. He also said the audit could take 15-20 days, while the timeline was not firmly committed.
Board has resolved to convert the company from a housing finance company to an NBFC; management said this takes at least 6 months and needs NOCs from all lenders.
Management said the company has no shortfall in operations and that promoters can infuse 100% of capital if needed.
capex_capacity: Slowdown in fresh sanctions and disbursements; part disbursements of existing sanctions continue, and the MD said he is slowing them further if needed.
Pending sanctions from banks are held until the red flag is removed.
Proposed NBFC conversion: management rejected a subsidiary route, saying the same work should not be done in two companies.
demand_pricing: Management said there is no shortage of demand and the slowdown is precautionary.
Management said there are zero promoter-related or related-party loans in the book.
No pricing, yield, or competitive commentary was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the account red flagged, and can a third-party re-inspection be commissioned?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD said the company does not know the reasons; NHB does not share them until the audit closes. He said a third-party re-inspection after the audit is 'not an issue'.

qa_highlights.question: Liquidity: what are monthly collections and cash balances?
qa_highlights.answer: Collections exceed obligations, but no figure was given. The MD said there is a 2-3 month repayment buffer, and that liquidity data was sent to the rating agency.

qa_highlights.question: Have lenders been told or has any recall happened?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it met each lender individually, that none has sought a recall, and that there has been no delay on any obligation.

qa_highlights.question: Did NHB communicate specific observations?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The MD said there has been no formal communication on the findings, and that observations from the last audit are internal and not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Can the promoter infuse capital if needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the MD said promoters can put in '100%' of required capital, but there is no current shortfall.

qa_highlights.question: Will you share collection efficiency and liquidity data regularly?
qa_highlights.answer: The MD said a liquidity statement was sent to the rating agency from March 2020; he declined to give the monthly collection amount and said he would send the liquidity position only up to March.

risks_watch: NHB red flag remains open; reasons and audit findings are not yet disclosed and no completion date is committed.
Acuite has placed the rating under watch; management says there is no downgrade.
Management provided no audited data on collections, NPAs, or the Rs 400 crore allegation; the 1,100 crore and 130 crore book figures given on the call are inconsistent.
Several lenders requested a group lender meeting; management said only 'we will see'.
Sanctions are on hold, and an RBI-mandated 90-day disbursement timeline was raised but not confirmed.
The NBFC conversion needs at least 6 months and lender NOCs; management gave no product or funding details.
summary.management_tone: Defensive and repetitive: management flatly denied all allegations and repeatedly deferred specifics to the pending audit. It gave no numbers on collections, liquidity, NPAs, or the audit timeline, and sometimes answered questions inconsistently (loan book Rs 130 crore vs Rs 1,100 crore).
key_quotes: We have a buffer of 2-3 months of repayment.
Our capital adequacy ratio is 39.21%, which is more than double the regulatory minimum.
We can put 100% capital in the company if need arises.
